chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj al-Karkhi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Zakat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever trading asset is in your hand where there is a profit, and nothing prevents you from selling it except that you seek to increase your profit (by holding it), then purify it (pay Zakat). And whatever trading asset is in your hand where there is a loss, that is another matter.'
ai.seo_question: How is Zakat calculated on trading goods held for profit versus those held for other reasons?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the criteria for Zakat on trade goods by distinguishing between assets held for speculative profit growth and those held for other purposes, such as utility or inevitable loss. This ruling establishes that the intention of accumulation (*ziyadah*) is the key determinant for Zakat liability in commercial transactions, a principle foundational to Shia jurisprudence on *Zakat al-Tijarah*. It underscores the ethical dimension of wealth, where hoarding for mere increase is subject to purification, while practical utility follows different rules.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym, from Khalid Bin Al Hajjjaj Al Karkhy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Zakāt, so heasws said: ‘Whatever was from a trading asset in your hand where is a profit, nothing preventing you from selling it except for the increase in profit (price) on top of your profit, so purify it (pay Zakāt) and whatever was from a trading asset in your hand wherein is a loss, so that is another thing’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj al-Karkhiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Zakat. He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever asset you have for doing business which increases and there is no obstacle for you to sell, except expecting increase over increase, then you must pay Zakat. Whatever you have for business in which there are losses then it is a different issue.’”
